desc:
React Native app maintenance and updates keep your app building, running and accepted by the stores as iOS, Android and libraries change. Ecom Swift LLC delivers a fixed starter sprint that updates packages, fixes warnings and ends with a clear health report.

## What is React Native app maintenance?

Maintenance is the regular work that keeps a finished app healthy. It includes updating dependencies, fixing build errors, answering new store requirements, reviewing crash reports and checking that the app still runs on current phones. It does not add new features.

Our starter sprint is a fixed one-time job. It brings the app up to date and gives you a written picture of its condition, so you know what to do next. Ongoing monthly care can be quoted separately.

## Why do apps break when nobody touches them?

An app is built on top of moving parts: the phone operating system, the React Native framework, native build tools and dozens of libraries. Each of them changes on its own schedule. After a year without updates, a project that once built fine may fail on a new computer, a new Xcode or a new Android toolchain.

Stores also change their requirements. A newer target Android level or an updated privacy label can block a release. Finding this out on the day you need to ship a fix is stressful and expensive.

## How regular updates protect users and budgets

Old libraries carry known security issues, and unmaintained ones eventually stop working. Updating in small, tested steps costs far less than a forced jump across many versions at once. Each skipped year makes the eventual catch-up larger.

Users notice the difference too. Fewer crashes, faster startup and correct layouts on new phones lead to better reviews and fewer support requests. Exact results depend on the app, but a maintained project is always cheaper to change than a neglected one.

## What a good care sprint includes

- A dependency check that lists outdated, deprecated and risky packages.
- Updates applied in small steps, with the app tested after each one.
- Fixes for build errors and warnings on iOS and Android.
- A review of crash reports for repeating problems.
- A check against current store requirements, such as target API level and privacy labels.
- A few real bugs fixed, chosen from your list or from the crash data.
- Performance quick wins where the cause is clear.
- An automated build set up in the larger package, so releases are repeatable.
- A health report that says what was done and what to do next.
- A six-month upkeep plan in the Premium package.

## What we do

We start by building the app as it stands and recording every error. Then we update packages in order of risk, running the app between steps. If a library has no working update, we suggest a replacement before changing it.

Basic covers a health check and the most urgent updates. Standard adds more packages, bug fixes and a store requirement check. Premium covers a full catch-up with a React Native version upgrade, bug fixes, performance quick wins, an automated build and the six-month plan. Every package ends with a written report.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Keep a list of bugs and complaints to hand over.
- Share your latest crash and store reports.
- Commit all work to your repository before we start.
- Test the updated build on a few real devices.
- Plan updates regularly, not only after something fails.

**Avoid:**
- Updating every package in one single step.
- Ignoring store emails about upcoming requirement changes.
- Leaving the app untouched for years because it works today.
- Mixing maintenance with a large redesign in the same release.
- Deleting old release builds before the update is confirmed.

## Who this service is for

An owner whose app no longer builds after a laptop or tool update. A business with a live app that has not been touched for a long time and wants to know the risk. A founder who inherited an app and needs a plain report on its condition before spending more.

## What we need from you

Repository access as a collaborator and your crash reports if you have them. If you want us to upload the update, add us to your store accounts with a limited developer role. We never need passwords, and we confirm the plan before we begin.
